summary: Iteration 3 verifies the tiered Shipping Depot contracts system + rare emergency contract. Backend GET /api/config exposes correct tiers (basic/scrap/L1/Easy/green, intermediate/components/L2/Medium/blue, advanced/finished_goods/L4/Hard/purple), tier_weights (3/2/2), emergency (enabled, finished_goods, 600s duration, 120s interval, 0.3 spawn_chance, L4, Rare, orange) and shipping_depot.quality.qty_per_level. PUT/GET round-trip preserves the new state shape (contracts[] with tier, emergency:{...expires_at}, emergency_next_check_ts). 9/9 backend pytest cases pass. Frontend Contracts screen at Lv1 correctly shows only 3 basic 'Local Delivery / Easy / Scrap' cards with per-card rewards visible before accepting; refresh works; disabled 'Not enough resources' button appears when material lacking. Depot upgrade sheet exposes both 'Contract Rewards' (+15% Coins & XP / lvl) and 'Contract Quality' (+20% order size / lvl) with the required testIDs. Higher-tier UI (Lv5 intermediate/advanced) and emergency card could not be forced through UI within test window: (a) direct localStorage injection of a level-5 save is overwritten by the remote save on boot (freshest-wins), and (b) emergency spawn is time-gated (0.3 chance every 120s, L4 only). Per agent-to-agent note, these are acceptable and validated via config + math + backend save/load. Reward-scaling math verified from config: advanced min payout is >5x basic min (72 vs 4 coins), making manufacturing worthwhile.
action_items: No blocking issues found. Optional: consider building an in-app dev tool ('Set Level' / 'Grant Materials' / 'Force Emergency') to make higher-tier + emergency scenarios testable without waiting on RNG. This would unblock full E2E coverage for future iterations.

Minor console warnings observed (not blockers): 'shadow* style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow' and 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Both come from RN core / app code and can be migrated at leisure.
critical_code_review_comments: engine.ts createDefaultState hard-codes generateBoardContract(1, ...) for the initial board. If a fresh normalizeState fallback (empty raw.contracts) triggers at high level, board is (harmlessly) regenerated at L1 mix on next fulfil. Acceptable, but consider passing state.level.
GameContext boot picks newer save between local & remote by last_seen_ts; injected local saves can be overwritten by remote if remote_ts >= local_ts. Fine for prod, but complicates test injection.
server.py GAME_CONFIG is >80 lines and lives in module scope; if it keeps growing, consider extracting to /app/backend/game_config.py for readability.

engine.ts tickContracts triggers a state update on every check-interval boundary even when no spawn (nextCheck is bumped). Correct behavior for gating, just be aware it dirties state and triggers persistence.
seed_data_creation: Test player_id TEST_tier_<ts> created and deleted within test_contracts_iter3.py::TestSaveLoadRoundtrip (self-cleanup).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_contracts_iter3.py — reuse. For future emergency/high-tier UI verification, either (a) add a dev tool button ('Grant Level', 'Grant Materials', 'Force Emergency'), or (b) mutate rbr_save_v1 in localStorage AND immediately DELETE /api/game/{player_id} before reload so the boot merge picks the local (higher-level) save. The player_id comes from localStorage['rbr_player_id'].
